title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 66 (Reduction of share capital)

content.overview: A limited company may reduce share capital by special resolution confirmed by the Tribunal, subject to creditor protection and the statutory bars.
content.glance: A limited company may reduce share capital by special resolution confirmed by the Tribunal, subject to creditor protection and the statutory bars.
content.study: Section 66 is the capital-maintenance gateway for reduction. The special resolution must be confirmed by the National Company Law Tribunal. The company must give notice to the Central Government, Registrar, SEBI in listed cases, and creditors as the Tribunal directs. The Tribunal considers creditor objections and may dispense with consent where debt is secured or discharged. Reduction cannot be used to extinguish liability on unpaid capital or to pay any paid-up capital where the company is in arrears of deposits or interest, except as the section allows. An order, once filed, is conclusive evidence of compliance. Accounting treatment must follow the prescribed standards; a reduction is not a buy-back under s. 68.

examples.title: Selective reduction
examples.body: A reduction extinguishing a class on fair terms still needs special resolution and NCLT confirmation.

examples.title: Deposit default
examples.body: A company in default of deposit repayment cannot use reduction to return paid-up capital except as s. 66 permits.

distinctions: Reduction (s. 66) needs Tribunal confirmation. Buy-back (s. 68) is a purchase of own securities under a different procedure. Forfeiture is an articles remedy for non-payment of calls, not a reduction order.

misconceptions.correction: A limited company may reduce share capital by special resolution confirmed by the Tribunal, subject to creditor protection and the statutory bars.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Is ROC filing alone enough to reduce capital?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Special resolution and Tribunal confirmation under s. 66 are required, followed by filing of the order.
